newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian CEC bank raises interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Romanian CEC bank raises interest rates.

text.p: Romanian state-owned Casa de Economii si Consemnatiuni SA (CEC) bank said on Monday it would lift its deposit and lending rates following an upward move of interest rates triggered by tougher monetary policies.
Starting February 1, the bank's sight deposit rates for individuals will rise by three points to an annual 18 percent, a CEC statement said on Monday.
Earlier in the day, another large Romanian bank, state-run Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA said it would raise term deposits rates starting Tuesday.
Over the past two weeks, several banks have announced rises in deposit rates following central bank moves to tighten monetary policy to calm inflation and prop the leu currency.
The CEC said its one-year rates would be raised by 14 percentage points to 54 percent, while its lending rates would go up to an annual 59 percent from 47 percent.
Deposits at the CEC -- a 135-year-old institution and formerly a savings bank -- rose by 25.5 percent last year to 2.5 trillion lei at the end of last December, CEC data showed.
Year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent last year, up from 27.8 percent in 1995 and almost triple the 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
The leu has fallen about 40 percent against the dollar since January 1. ($=5,677 lei)
